flagged.title: Context: Romanticism, Science & the Gothic
flagged.reason: The video states and displays on screen that both Part (a) and Part (b) assess AO1 and AO2, which would lead students to waste exam time analysing methods in Part (b) where AO2 receives zero marks.

mark_affecting.quote: Both parts are testing you on your AO1 and AO2 skills.

flagged.title: The Creature's Story
flagged.reason: The video presents Milton's quote 'Evil, be thou my good' directly in the Creature's speech bubble, teaching an incorrect line from another text rather than the Creature's actual line ('Evil thenceforth became my good'), which costs quotation marks in a closed-book GCSE exam.

mark_affecting.quote: On-screen speech bubble: 'Evil, be thou my good.' Audio: 'he directly echoes Satan's famous declaration from Paradise Lost: Evil, be thou my good.'

flagged.title: The Pursuit & the Ending
flagged.reason: The video presents the fabricated quotation analysis (F9), telling students that 'blot' and 'wretch' are specific words used in the Creature's final speech, which would lead students to misattribute quotations in GCSE exam essays.

mark_affecting.quote: Listen to the specific, grade-boosting vocabulary the creature uses to describe himself in his devastating final speech. He uses three specific words: an abortion, a blot, and a wretch.

flagged.title: Key Themes & Exam Technique
flagged.reason: The video incorrectly teaches that both Part (a) and Part (b) of the Edexcel exam assess AO1 and AO2, whereas Part (a) is assessed solely on AO2 and Part (b) solely on AO1, directly compromising exam preparation and mark attainment.

mark_affecting.quote: Task: Extract | AO: 1 & 2; Task: Wider | AO: 1 & 2 ... This hits AO1, your understanding, and AO2, your language analysis ... Both tasks heavily assess your ability to pull ideas together and analyze how Shelley is actually writing.
Task: Extract | AO: 1 & 2 ... This hits AO1, your understanding, and AO2, your language analysis.
